title: Thai VAT Recognition: correct the customer party fields on the VAT accounts
description:
The port of the Thai VAT Recognition controller into Print Designer inherited a latent bug of the original TBS implementation: create_vat_gl_entry() sets party_type "Customer" and party <customer> on both the debit row (VAT receivable / input VAT) and the credit row (VAT payable / output VAT).

Under ERPNext that is invalid:
- erpnext/accounts/party.py:806 validate_account_party_type() allows party_type and party only on Receivable, Payable or Equity accounts. A Tax, Current Asset or Current Liability account with a party throws "Party Type and Party can only be set for Receivable / Payable account".
- erpnext/accounts/doctype/journal_entry/journal_entry.py:591 validate_party() requires party_type and party on Receivable and Payable rows unless party_not_required is set, and it refuses a party type whose account type differs from the account type.
- erpnext/accounts/doctype/gl_entry/gl_entry.py:276 calls the same validation.

The Thai chart of accounts places Input VAT under Assets > Current Assets > Other Current Assets > Value Added Tax and Output VAT under Liabilities > Current Liabilities > Other Current Liabilities, so neither account is a Receivable or a Payable account. The inherited party assignment therefore makes the Journal Entry impossible to post.

Correct behaviour: attach the customer party only where ERPNext permits it, based on the account type of the target account. The correction takes precedence over reproducing the TBS behaviour bug for bug.

The fix needs a disposable, ERPNext valid account fixture in the tests (the demo site has no %VAT%Receivable% or %VAT%Payable% leaf account and the Company fields default_input_vat_account / default_output_vat_account are unset). The fixture must respect validate_parent, validate_parent_child_account_type, set_root_and_report_type and the fact that Account.on_trash() refuses deletion when GL entries exist.
close_reason: Fixed in the Print Designer port: the rows of the journal entry of the recognition carry no party, and party_not_required is set only when a site models a VAT account as a receivable or a payable. The tests use disposable Current Asset / Current Liability accounts inside a savepoint, so the site keeps no account, no entry of the ledger and no trace of the tests. print_designer.tests.test_thai_vat_recognition: 16 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors; the whole app: 564 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 4 skipped.

title: Milestone invoice: concurrent generation can create a duplicate invoice
description:
The milestones were partitioned from the Sales Order document as it was loaded, before the row lock was taken. Two requests that generate the invoices at the same time could both read the same milestone as "not invoiced yet" and both create an invoice for it.

The fix re-reads the milestone rows under the row lock (`select ... from tabInvoice Schedule where parent = %s for update`) after `_lock_sales_order(doc.name)`, and refreshes the milestone status, the invoice link, the invoice date and the portion of every row. A milestone that another request claimed in the meantime is then skipped instead of being billed twice.

Regression test: `print_designer/tests/test_invoice_schedule_flow.py::test_a_milestone_that_was_claimed_in_the_meantime_is_not_billed_again`. The test fails with `2 != 1` when the locked refresh is removed.
notes: Fixed in print_designer/custom/invoice_schedule.py: _refresh_milestone_rows(doc) re-reads the milestone rows under the row lock after _lock_sales_order, so a milestone that another request claimed in the meantime is skipped instead of billed twice.
close_reason: Fixed: the milestone rows are re-read under the row lock after the Sales Order lock is taken, so a milestone that another request claimed in the meantime is skipped instead of billed twice. Covered by test_a_milestone_that_was_claimed_in_the_meantime_is_not_billed_again.

title: Milestone invoice: ERPNext re-derives the line rate from margin and pricing rules
description:
The milestone rate is derived from the contract: `rate = so_item.rate * invoice_portion / 100`. ERPNext works the rate of a Sales Invoice line out again from the price list, the pricing rules and the margin of the line (`erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py::calculate_margin`).

The ERPNext mapper copies `margin_type`, `margin_rate_or_amount` and `pricing_rules` from the Sales Order line onto the Sales Invoice line. So the margin of the contract line was applied a second time on top of the milestone rate and the invoice billed more than the milestone.

Measured on the demo site with a contract of 10 @ 1,100 = 11,000 (price list rate 10,000, margin 10% which ERPNext turned into an amount margin of 1,000) and a 40% milestone:

- before the fix: invoice line 10 @ 5,400 = 54,000
- after the fix:  invoice line 10 @ 4,400 = 44,000 (= 40% of 11,000)

`Sales Invoice` has no `ignore_pricing_rule` field, so the margin and the pricing rules are cleared on the generated line instead. The milestone rate is derived from the contract, not priced, so those inputs do not belong on the line.

Regression test: `print_designer/tests/test_invoice_schedule_flow.py::test_a_margin_on_the_order_line_is_not_applied_a_second_time`. The test fails with `5400.0 != 4400.0` when the fix is removed.
notes: Fixed in print_designer/custom/invoice_schedule.py (_build_milestone_invoice): the generated milestone line clears margin_type, margin_rate_or_amount and pricing_rules, so ERPNext does not price the already scaled milestone rate a second time.
close_reason: Fixed: the generated milestone line clears margin_type, margin_rate_or_amount and pricing_rules, so ERPNext does not apply the contract line's margin a second time on top of the milestone rate. Covered by test_a_margin_on_the_order_line_is_not_applied_a_second_time.

title: [BUG] PDF download endpoint bypassed the Chrome pipeline (no header/footer merge, no page numbers)
description:

title: The cancellation of the certificate commits the transaction of the caller
description: The on_cancel of the controller of the certificate (print_designer/print_designer/doctype/withholding_tax_certificate/withholding_tax_certificate.py) ends with frappe.db.commit(). A document hook that commits commits everything that is pending in the transaction of the caller, not only the certificate: a cancellation of a payment entry that cancels its certificate in the same flow can therefore persist a half finished work, and the savepoints of the caller are destroyed. The clearing of the link does not need the commit, it belongs to the transaction of the request. The proof: the test of the cancellation (print_designer/tests/test_wht_certificate_cancellation.py) could not roll back its rows with a savepoint, and the run left three cancelled certificates on the demo site until they were removed; the test now removes its rows one by one and commits at the end. Removing the commit keeps the behavior of the clearing and restores the atomicity, but it is a change of the transaction semantics of a document of a client, so it waits for the word of the owner of the app.
notes:
The commit of the on_cancel is removed. The cleanup of the cancellation is unchanged: the flag, the removal of the item of the form of the tax, the reading of the name of the payment entry, the clearing of the link of the certificate, the clearing of the reverse link and the direct SQL. The end of the method carries a comment that states why the work belongs to the caller. The commit of make_payment_entry_editable is a separate matter and was left alone.

The transaction boundary of every entry point belongs to Frappe: the request commits or rolls back in frappe/app.py::sync_database, the background job in frappe/utils/background_jobs.py::execute_job, the bench command in frappe/commands/utils.py. A controller that commits takes the boundary away from its owner and makes the work of the caller impossible to undo.

The test of the cancellation leans on a savepoint now. The test that guards the rule is a probe: it takes a savepoint before the cancellation and rolls back to it afterwards, because a commit takes the savepoint of the caller with it. The teardown keeps the removal of the rows one by one as a fallback, so the site stays clean even when the defect is present.

The proof that the probe can fail: the commit was put back into the controller temporarily and the test was run against it. The result was SUMMARY 4 1 0, the probe failed with "the cancellation of the certificate committed the transaction of the caller: (1305, SAVEPOINT wht_certificate_cancellation_probe does not exist)". The other three tests of the module passed with the commit in place, because the commit does not change the outcome of the cancellation itself. The controller was restored byte identically afterwards.

The verification of the change: ruff check and ruff format --check are clean on the controller and the test, basedpyright reports 0 errors and 0 warnings on both, the focused WHT batch is SUMMARY 63 0 0, the full Print Designer suite on [site] is SUMMARY 751 0 0, and the site keeps no row of the test afterwards.

The documentation is in wiki/wht-certificate-cancellation-transaction-minimax.md and in AGENTS.md.
close_reason: The commit of the on_cancel is removed, the cancellation takes part in the transaction of the caller, and the probe test of the savepoint proves that the controller commits nothing of its own.

title: The tax id and the address of a party that is not a supplier
description: The tax id of the certificate is read from the Supplier and the address only from a supplier. A payment entry that pays another kind of party therefore leaves supplier_tax_id and supplier_address empty, while the forms of the tax of the revenue department ask for the tax id of the payee. The alternatives are a tax id of the kind of the party, a fallback to the link of the certificate, or a wider field on the payment entry. The evidence of the legacy model of the client (that app/that app/that app/doctype/withholding_tax_cert/): its client read the tax id, the branch code and the address of the payee only when the party of the payment entry was a supplier (pe.party_type === 'Supplier'), its controller checked the tax id of the payee only when there was one (if self.payee_tax_id), and the certificate that the server created took the tax id of the supplier. The rule of today is therefore the rule of the legacy model; the question is whether it shall be widened. The current behavior is proven by print_designer/tests/test_wht_certificate_income_type_rules.py and described in wiki/wht-certificate-income-type-rules-minimax.md. Nothing changes until the rule is decided.
close_reason: Decided: the question does not reach the canonical certificate, so the rule stays as it is and no code changes. The certificate of the canonical model is the certificate of an outgoing withholding, the payment to a supplier. The creator refuses a payment entry whose party is not a supplier (print_designer/custom/wht_certificate_creator.py), and that refusal is proven by test_a_payment_entry_of_another_party_creates_no_certificate of print_designer/tests/test_wht_certificate_creator.py. The field supplier of the certificate is a mandatory link to Supplier, so a certificate cannot exist without a supplier. The incoming withholding of Thailand is the Receive WHT Register, a doctype of its own, so the tax id of a customer is never printed on a certificate of this model. The tax id and the address of the certificate are therefore read from the Supplier alone, which is the rule of the legacy model, and there is nothing to widen. Recorded in wiki/wht-certificate-income-type-rules-minimax.md.

title: The rate of the parent of a mixed certificate
description: The certificate of the withholding tax shows the rate of its first row of the incomes next to the income type of the transaction. A transaction that mixes two rates and two kinds of income therefore shows a rate that does not belong to its income type. The alternatives are the rate of the type of the transaction, a weighted rate, or no rate on the parent of a mixed transaction. The evidence of the legacy model of the client (that app/that app/that app/doctype/withholding_tax_cert/): its controller never wrote the rate of the document, it wrote only the tax of every row and the totals; the client of the legacy document wrote the rate of the document out of a map of the fourteen codes, with the income type of the document as its key; the rows took their rate from the payment entry (dgs_custom_wht_rate) and from their own income type. The rate of the parent therefore never followed the rows in the legacy model, and the income type of the parent was a choice of the hand there. The rule of the first row is new and has no legacy precedent; the legacy rule was the rate follows the income type of the parent, which in the canonical model would become the rate of the catalogue of the type of the transaction. The current behavior is proven by print_designer/tests/test_wht_certificate_income_type_rules.py and described in wiki/wht-certificate-income-type-rules-minimax.md. Nothing changes until the rule is decided.
close_reason: Decided and implemented: the rate of the certificate is the rate of the catalogue of the income type of the transaction, not the rate of the first row of the incomes. The legacy model wrote the rate of the document out of a map of the income types with the income type of the document as its key, and the rows took their own rate from the payment entry, so the rate of the parent never followed the rows. The rows keep their own rate; an income type that carries no rate of its own falls back to the rate of the first row. Implemented in print_designer/custom/wht_certificate_creator.py (build_certificate_values). Proven by print_designer/tests/test_wht_certificate_income_type_rules.py, with a negative proof that the old rule fails the new coverage. title: The status of the certificate drifts from the state of the document
description: The field status of the canonical Withholding Tax Certificate is written when the certificate is created ('Issued' by the creator). The controller of the certificate does not move it when the certificate is submitted or cancelled, so a certificate that is created outside the creator keeps 'Draft' forever. The vocabulary of the field allows Draft, Issued, Submitted to Revenue Dept and Cancelled. Which of them the field shall carry after a submit and after a cancel is a decision of the product, not of a refactoring; the report readers that filter on the status have to be checked against the decision. The live data of the client site, read only on 2026-11-23, shows the drift in all its forms: the eight mirrored certificates are submitted (docstatus 1) and say 'Issued', WHTC-6906-00005 is submitted (docstatus 1) and says 'Draft', and the four cancelled ones (docstatus 2) still say 'Issued' or 'Draft'. The legacy model of the client had the vocabulary Draft, Submitted and Cancelled, and it wrote 'Submitted' when it created the certificate and submitted it (that app/setup/service_wht_payments.py); the legacy controller never moved the status on submit, so the legacy status was written once, at the creation. The canonical writer already matches the legacy word for the submitted case ('Issued' is the canonical word for the legacy 'Submitted'); what is missing is the move of the status on a submit of a draft certificate and on a cancel.

description: The legacy Withholding Tax Cert is gone as a doctype; the canonical model of Print Designer carries every record of the client already: eight of the thirteen legacy rows are mirrored in the canonical Withholding Tax Certificate and the five incoming rows are mirrored in the canonical Receive WHT Register, with the same certificate number, the same dates, the same amounts, the same rate and the same payment entry. The decision, the mapping of every field and the plan are written in wiki/wht-legacy-retirement-and-field-mapping-minimax.md. title: Apply the reviewed Output VAT Undue ledger migration on an authorized site and validate it live
description:
The ledger of the Output VAT Undue is implemented and reviewed, but neither [site] nor [site] carries the new schema or metadata: both hold the legacy metadata, the legacy table (28 columns, primary key on the name only) and no row at all.

Required, with an explicit authorization of the user:
1. Run the model synchronisation of the app on the chosen site, so that the expanded columns and the naming of the document exist.
2. Run print_designer.patches.migrate_output_vat_undue_ledger and read its report.
3. Verify the constraint of the table with SHOW INDEX FROM "tabOutput VAT Undue" (the name of the index differs between the adapters).
4. Create a service Sales Invoice on the site and check the row of the ledger: one row per invoice, the name of the row is the name of the invoice, the snapshot of the decision, no GL entry.
5. Confirm that the legacy rows of the site keep their names and their values, and that the migration creates no row and no GL entry for the history.

Nothing of this may run without the authorization of the user: the model synchronisation and the migration write to the database of a site.
notes:
Status 2026-11-22: the demo site is migrated and verified. On [site] the model synchronisation was applied and print_designer.patches.migrate_output_vat_undue_ledger ran: autoname is field:sales_invoice, allow_rename is 0, the metadata carries 39 DocFields, the table carries 41 physical columns, the only physical indexes are PRIMARY (name) and creation, there is no unique index on sales_invoice, and the table holds no row - the migration created no historical tracking and no GL entry. The patch reports nothing on a second run. The site level tests of the ledger run on that site now: print_designer.tests.test_output_vat_undue_tracking reports 34 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; the full app reports 521 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 4 skipped.

Two defects were found and fixed while the migration ran: the report of the rows without a snapshot called frappe.db.sql() without as_dict=True and crashed on the tuple, and the options of the Select field service_classification were written with another case than the constants of the contract (Services against services), so the classification of a row could not be stored.

The treatment of an invoice is resolved by the site itself: the Thai Business Suite apply_vat_treatment() writes it while the invoice is saved and overwrites a manual VAT Undue with the treatment of the tax template of the company. The ledger reads the persisted treatment, so the row of the demo site carries VAT Due and the status Already Due. The site level test expects the decision of the invoice and not a reason of its own; the matrix of the reasons stays covered by the unit tests of the contract.

Remaining: the same run on [site]. It needs a separate explicit authorization, it writes to the database of the site, and the ledger of that site still carries the legacy metadata, the legacy table and no row.

The design question of the migration is answered on 2026-11-22: no phase before the model synchronisation is needed. The unique index of a field comes from the property unique of the field and the field sales_invoice does not carry it, so the synchronisation creates no unique index on the column and cannot fail because of the rows that share an invoice; the primary key is the name of the row, the rows of the old implementation carry a name of their own and the history is not rewritten, so the synchronisation cannot fail because of them either. The invoices that share more than one row are settled where they matter: the writer looks for the row of the invoice before it writes one and the reader takes the oldest row of the invoice as the row of the ledger. The patch stays a post model patch; the reconciliation of the history of the ledger (a backfill of the snapshot) remains a job of its own. Detail in wiki/si-services-output-vat-undue-minimax.md and in the docstring of the patch.

title: Milestone invoice: percent column and full service quantity
description:
The milestone invoices of a Sales Order carry a visible percent column, and a
milestone bills a part of the contract instead of a part of the service.

Field
- Sales Invoice Item -> pd_custom_invoice_portion, Percent, label "%",
  read only, insert_after amount, in_list_view. It sits right after the
  Amount column of the invoice.
- Installed by print_designer/commands/install_milestone_invoice_item_fields.py,
  registered in after_migrate and removed again on uninstall.

Semantics
- A milestone bills a part of the contract and does not deliver a part of the
  service, so the quantity stays the contract quantity and the rate carries the
  portion: rate = so_item.rate * invoice_portion / 100.
- ERPNext works the line amount out as qty * rate, so a line that keeps
  "40 @ 7,500" while storing 60,000 is not a stable Frappe state. The
  contractual derivation is written into the item description.
- The submission guard compares the quantity, the portion and the amount, it
  never compares the rate.

Evidence on the demo site for a 40 @ 7,500 = 300,000 contract with the
milestones 20/60/20: three draft invoices of 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000,
40 @ 4,500 = 180,000 and 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000. The invoices total 300,000, the
order reaches per_billed 100 and the Sales Order line reaches billed_amt
300,000, so no overbilling was booked.
A real browser run confirms the percent column of the invoice line and the
values 10 @ 200 = 2,000 with 20.00% on a disposable fixture.

Open
- The field is not installed on [site] yet, that needs the
  authorization of the site owner.

title: Milestone invoice amounts ignore the discount and the price list
description: print_designer/custom/invoice_schedule.py::_build_milestone_invoice builds the invoice line from the Sales Order line: it keeps the contract quantity, scales the rate by the milestone portion, copies the price list rate and zeroes discount_percentage and discount_amount. ERPNext works the amount out itself in calculate_taxes_and_totals and re-derives the rate from the price list and the pricing rules, so on a line with a price list, a discount percentage, a pricing rule or taxes the invoice no longer adds up to the milestone amount that the Sales Order shows. The milestone amounts are taken from the contract net_total, which is net of the discount, while the invoice line is gross, so the two drift apart. Fix: let ERPNext calculate the invoice and take the milestone amount from the resulting invoice, or map the price list and the discount fields so ERPNext reproduces the contract amount.
close_reason: Fixed. ERPNext no longer prices the milestone rate a second time: the generated line clears margin_type, margin_rate_or_amount and pricing_rules and keeps the scaled milestone rate in price_list_rate, so the invoice line is exactly the milestone share of the contract line. The price list, the discount and the pricing rule part of this report is the same defect as print_designer-lh4. Measured on the demo site with a 7% VAT item, a contract of 10 @ 1,000 = 10,000 (net_total 10,000, VAT 700, total 10,700) and a 40% milestone: the invoice line is 10 @ 400 = 4,000 with VAT 280, the invoice net_total is 4,000 and the invoice total is 4,280. The milestone row amount (net_total * portion / 100 = 4,000) is the invoice net_total, so the milestone and the invoice no longer drift apart, and the submission guard accepts the invoice.

title: The print view stops when the process does not work in the directory of the sites
description:
The print view of the app stops when the process does not work in the directory of the sites.

The template is print_designer/www/printview.html, and the eighth line is
`{{ include_style('print.bundle.css') }}`.  The style of the bundle is asked for in
frappe/utils/jinja_globals.py::bundled_asset, and the assets of the site are read by
frappe.utils.get_assets_json(), which reads `assets/assets.json` with a path that is relative to
the working directory of the process.  The assets of the site live in sites/assets/assets.json, so
they are found only when the process works in the directory of the sites.  When they are not found,
the failure is `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`, and every print of the
site stops with it.

The proof on the running site, with the same site and the same document: the print of a Customer
renders (26085 characters) from /home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites, and stops with the error from
/home/frappe/frappe-bench.

The services of the bench are not the cause: the working directory of the web, of the two workers
and of the scheduler was read from /proc, and it is /home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites in all of
them.  The cause is a process that works elsewhere: a console, a test runner, a job that was
started from the root of the bench.

Two ways to repair it, and the choice is not made yet:
- the core of Frappe reads the assets of the site with the path of the site
  (frappe.get_site_path("assets/assets.json")) and not with a path that is relative to the
  working directory;
- the print view of the app asks for the style of the bundle with a URL of the site and not with
  include_style.

The M Capital app no longer loses its Loan Screening when this happens, and the tests of the app
run where the services run: see the tracker of the M Capital app, that app-izup.

title: [BUG] Exported Print Designer templates fail to render: frappe.parse_json missing in the Jinja sandbox
description: Exported Print Designer templates embed their design (header/body/footer/settings) as a JSON blob and parse it at render time with {% set __pd_data = frappe.parse_json("...") %}. Verified live: the Sales Invoice - TBS Standard format now renders - HTTP 200, a valid 1 page PDF with the invoice content, no parse_json error (previously it failed). title: Thailand WHT helper is never loaded: pd_apply_item_wht_config is not defined
description:
The Thailand WHT helper is not available when the form needs it, so every
Sales Invoice, Sales Order and Quotation reports a runtime error in the
browser.

pd_apply_item_wht_config is defined in
print_designer/public/js/thailand_wht/thailand_wht_vat_helper.js and used in

- print_designer/public/js/thailand_wht/thailand_wht_sales_invoice.js
- print_designer/public/js/thailand_wht/thailand_wht_quotation.js
- print_designer/public/js/thailand_wht/thailand_wht_sales_order.js

The doctype_js hook loads the helper for those forms, but the app bundle
print_designer/public/js/app.js imports thailand_wht_sales_invoice directly,
so the module runs before the asynchronously loaded doctype_js script has
evaluated. The browser run on [site] reports the page error
"pd_apply_item_wht_config is not defined" on the Sales Invoice form.

The fix is to import the helper from app.js before the modules that use it,
so the dependency is static. The site needs a rebuild of the app bundle
afterwards.

title: Milestone invoice of a stock item should prorate the quantity
description:
The milestone invoices keep the contract quantity and carry the portion of the
contract in the rate of the line.

For a service item this is right, a service has no stock and a milestone does
not deliver a part of the service. For a stock item the quantity is normally
prorated by the portion, because a milestone of goods delivers a part of the
quantity.

Evidence on the demo site for a 40 @ 7,500 = 300,000 contract with the
milestones 20/60/20: three draft invoices of 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000,
40 @ 4,500 = 180,000 and 40 @ 1,500 = 60,000. The invoices total 300,000, the
order reaches per_billed 100 and the Sales Order line reaches billed_amt
300,000, so no overbilling was booked.
